purpose: OPERATOR REFERENCE ONLY — never used as design DNA. Template is the sole source of layout and structure.
strengths: Real photography throughout — providers, patients, procedure imagery. No stock-looking gradients.
Insurance carrier logos (Aetna, Cigna, Humana, UnitedHealthcare, Ambetter, Blue Cross Blue Shield) are displayed prominently — strong trust signal worth carrying forward.
Three attributed patient reviews with 5-star marks are on the homepage.
Address, business hours, and social links are all present in the footer.
Deep condition and procedure coverage — roughly 90 individual condition/procedure pages exist behind the nav.
weaknesses: Navigation is overwhelming: a 90+ item mega-menu across SERVICES, PROCEDURES, and RESOURCES with no clear primary path. A patient in pain has to parse four nested lists to find anything.

No conversion path above the fold beyond a single 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT' button — no phone number visible in the hero, no 'accepting new patients' or 'same-day appointments' message anywhere on the homepage.
The strongest true differentiators (same-day appointments, accepting new patients, board-certified physician) are buried on the FAQ page and never surface on the homepage.
Page is extremely long (~7,500px) with duplicated desktop/mobile content blocks rendered in the same DOM, which bloats the page and repeats sections visually.
Two competing phone numbers (new patients vs existing patients) are only reachable through a modal on the contact page — a new patient cannot find a number to call from the homepage.
Dense dark-navy blocks stacked back-to-back with low contrast body copy hurt readability for an older patient demographic.
Aggressive 'You cannot copy content of this website, your IP is being recorded' banner appears in page content — reads as hostile to visitors.
Third-party vendor widgets (onrevenue.us, hipaaserver2.us) drive text/chat/appointment flows; an AI chat assistant is self-labeled 'in Beta testing, so I can make mistakes' on a medical site.
load_issues: Homepage renders both desktop and mobile variants of most sections in the same document rather than swapping via CSS breakpoints, roughly doubling image payload.
carry_forward: Three attributed patient testimonials → Testimonials section
The five homepage-prioritized conditions (Back, Neck, Joint, Nerve, CRPS) → the five service pages
Six named service-area towns → service-area pages
